Pass 4 overlay (Mercator, rhumb-line legs) of COLREG.2/Circ.55 annex 6 positions (ED50): separation zones, inshore traffic zone and all lanes except the outermost southbound (dangerous cargo) lane lie inside. reporting_boundary_basis: COPREP (MSC.278(85)): TSS not named. vts_name: Salvamento Marítimo CCS Cartagena maritime traffic service (Cartagena port STM and observed Cabo de Palos DST watch)
vts_boundary_basis: CCS Cartagena is a SASEMAR centre that operates a contracted port maritime traffic service (STM) for the Cartagena Port Authority with VTS-trained controllers (SRC-2214, SRC-2011, SRC-2213), so it is a VTS-type centre in the same sense as CCS Almería (VTS-0202). Its only statutory service area is port waters: Zona II ends at the Punta del Sofre to Cabo Tiñoso line (SRC-2218); recomputed, vertex L-2 (37 33.5 N 000 57.3 W, ED50 UTM converted) lies 17.1 NM from the nearest TSS vertex, and about 12 NM even if the inshore zone is carried to the coast at Cabo de Palos; the ED50 to WGS84 shift is about 0.1 NM, so the port area clearly does not reach the TSS. The link therefore rests on monitoring by a VTS centre (decision 1): a Government Delegation statement, reported in September 2024 (SRC-2125), that CCS Cartagena detected a vessel contravening the Cabo de Palos DST, called it on VHF 16, and that the Capitanía opened sanction proceedings; Tramos (SRC-096), an official ministry publication written by SASEMAR, lists Cabo de Palos among Spain's DST and says the DST are controlled by the STM/VTS function assigned to SASEMAR; RD 210/2004 (SRC-2215) gives the CCS a general duty to follow ships using IMO routeing systems.
reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system (baseline list). Spain's official statements (SASEMAR DST page; Tramos Feb 2025) list mandatory reporting only at Finisterre, the Strait of Gibraltar and the Canarias PSSA.

evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: No candidate service reaches or is assigned to the TSS. Port services, recomputed on official polygons: Alicante Zona II (current, Orden TRM/361/2025, ETRS89) nearest vertex 35.4 NM from the nearest TSS vertex, about 30 NM even if the inshore zone is taken to Ifach (SRC-2219); Gandía Zona II (Autoridad Portuaria de Valencia, Orden TRM/357/2024) 25.7 NM, about 17 NM even to Cape San Antonio (SRC-2220); Valencia port lies further north. Datum effects (ED50 to WGS84 about 0.1 NM) are negligible against these margins. SASEMAR scope: SASEMAR's own current statements of where it monitors DST traffic list Finisterre, Tarifa, Cabo de Gata and Canarias only (SRC-2022, SRC-2213, SRC-2011), no CCS is assigned a Cabo de la Nao task, and no SASEMAR port traffic contract exists for Valencia, Alicante or Dénia (SRC-2011). This meets the negative standard of an authority source expressly stating the relevant service scope plus official boundaries excluding nearby port services. The Tramos sentence that 'the DST are controlled by the STM' (SRC-096) is generic: the same article's lead paragraph names the DST SASEMAR controls and omits La Nao, and unlike Palos there is no report of any centre watching or acting in this TSS, so it does not identify a service or amount to a contrary official statement for La Nao. | Earlier record: FC-A VTS finding: None established. The TSS (38 37.7 N to 38 44.0 N, 000 13.5 E to 000 28.8 E) is roughly 40 NM or more from Alicante and Valencia. | Earlier record: No mandatory reporting (Spain's official list of mandatory systems excludes Cabo de la Nao; no Part I system). evidence_summary: FC-A VTS finding: Supplemental (not core VTS). In-force Prémar arrêté 256/2016 (SRC-2131, SRC-2132), made specifically for the Corsica Channel TSS, gives a standing shore role: art. 7 requires VHF 16 watch throughout passage in the part of the TSS and precautionary areas in French territorial waters and in the ZNC, and a duty to answer CROSS Méditerranée or a sémaphore and to keep watch on the channel they indicate; art. 4 and 6 require reports to the Cap Corse or Sagro sémaphore on entering the ZNC; art. 5 requires annual declarations to CROSS Méditerranée; art. 8 lets the préfet maritime impose routing or order a vessel to divert. This meets the prompt's supplemental category (monitoring/information service associated with a TSS, not confirmed as a formal VTS). Current operation is corroborated by lead sources: 2025 briefing reporting that CROSS Med oversees compliance with the canal de Corse DST and that Sagro surveils traffic in the channel (SRC-2143), and an April 2025 Prémar communiqué, reported in the press, on Sagro alerting and reinforcing surveillance of a ship in the DST (SRC-2144). Not a VTS: the June 2026 ministry press kit gives VTS functions to the Channel CROSS only (SRC-2014), so decision 1 does not make it core. Coverage Partial: the statutory watch and answer duty applies only in the French territorial-sea part of the TSS, which the arrêté fixes on the equidistance line between Cap Corse and Capraia (about the separation zone axis, 009°37'E to 009°40'E, so roughly the southbound lane and the western precautionary areas; exact line not computed); the Italian (northbound) side has no Italian VTS (SRC-2133 to SRC-2137). | Earlier record: TSS identity confirmed (COLREG.2/Circ.67, in force 1 Dec 2016). No Part I scheme; no VTS established by official source.
source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.67 (20 May 2016); French DP 60 ans des CROSS (3 Jun 2026); MIT release (3 Nov 2015, modified 20 Dec 2022)
unresolved_issue: None for the classification. Coordinate rounding (0.1' is at most about 0.1 nm) plus any residual datum error (both sources declare WGS 84; even an undeclared ED50 or Roma 40 origin would shift positions by roughly 0.05 to 0.1 nm here) totals about 0.15 to 0.2 nm, well inside the 0.58 nm minimum margin. Venice VTS (operational, on the national list of 11 centres) does not cover this TSS: its own manual lists the IMO scheme as outside the VTS area, and coordinates show it ends about 1 nm outside the outer limit. Vessels must call Venice VTS 5 NM before the outer limit, which may fall inside the TSS, but this is a first-call point, not evidence of monitoring the scheme.

The only IMO scheme in the approaches to Piraeus is TSS-0111, whose IMO title is 'in the approaches to Piraeus Harbour' (separation zone from about 6 nm to 17 nm south of the harbour), and the vessel traffic control function of the Piraeus authority is exercised through VTS Piraeus. NGA Pub. 132 (2026, lead only) independently states that a VTS 'is established in the approaches to Piraievs'. The 2003 VTMIS regulation defines areas in annexes, but its published annexes cover only the Ionian centres, so no official Piraeus polygon exists to test. No official source places the scheme outside VTS Piraeus.

tss_name: In the approaches to Ras Tanura and Ju’aymah
vts_name: Ras Tanura Vessel Traffic Management System (Ras Tanura VTMS)
vts_authority: Saudi Aramco (Manager, Port Operations, Port of Ras Tanura)
vts_centre: Ras Tanura Port Control (Ras Tanura Port Control Center)
vts_boundary_basis: Aramco July 2025 book: the VTMS is mandatory 'for all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura'. The 11-point harbour boundary has its eastern limit on 50 23 E between 27 00 N and 27 12 N. The IMO scheme (A.338(IX) as amended) runs from 50 42 E west to the Ras Tanura channel at about 26 41 N 50 12 E. The Ju'aymah departure lane (Part III) runs east along 27 11.5 N to 50 36 E. Inside the port limits: the channel section, the Ju'aymah approach lane and the western end of the departure lane. Outside them: the eastern approach lanes (about 50 23 E to 50 42 E) and the eastern part of the Ju'aymah departure lane (50 23 E to 50 36 E). Pub. 172 (2025) lists VTMS reporting to Ras Tannurah Port Control from Ras Tannurah Lighted Buoy (27 06 N 50 57 E), east of the scheme, and the Aramco speed rules apply to all ships 'using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme' from the Approach Buoy. So traffic in the whole scheme is in contact with the service. The service's defined area is still the port. Hence partial. The service is a VTS in its own right: it is a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service, so the decision 5 fallback is not needed.
reporting_boundary_basis: Not in IMO Part I. Reports to Ras Tanura Port Control (Entry buoy, A buoy, anchoring, departure) are routine VTMS reporting and form part of the VTS, not a separate MRS. No national mandatory reporting scheme found in Pub. 172 (2025) or the Aramco book.
evidence_summary: Aramco's July 2025 port book describes a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service. It covers all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura and states that the Ras Tanura Channel separation zones and routes are IMO-approved. Speed and reporting rules apply to 'all ships using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme'. The port boundary includes the channel and Ju'aymah parts of the TSS but not the eastern approach lanes between about 50 23 E and 50 42 E. Pub. 172 (2025) confirms the VTMS covers Ras Tannurah and the Ju Aymah terminals and lists reporting points along the approach. It is an official port traffic management service (decision 5), with partial coverage.
source_date: Aramco Ports and Terminals July 2025; NGA Pub. 172 24th ed. 2025; IMO A.338(IX) 1975
unresolved_issue: The current IMO 2025 geometry has not been checked against A.338(IX) (1975, 'as amended'); later amendments may move the eastern end. VTMS coverage of the eastern lanes beyond the port limit rests only on reporting points, not on a defined service area.
vts_coverage_type: Partial TSS coverage; see boundary basis

evidence_summary: The scheme was adopted by MSC 69 (COLREG.2/Circ.44, in force 1 December 1998). The first-pass 'offshore laden-tanker system' is routeing guidance, not a VTS or reporting scheme. SAFREP covers the area but SAMSA states that participation is voluntary (MN 35 of 2018), so it is not an MRS.

unresolved_issue: The exact Sector 1/2 boundary latitude is read from a small-scale chartlet (about 02 52 N); it does not affect the result because both sectors are Klang VTS. A Marine Department Malaysia primary page for Klang VTS was not opened; current operation rests on MPA (2026) and Pub. 174 (2025).

review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. The MPA page (updated 30 September 2026) names Klang VTS for Sectors 1 and 2. The Circ.44 annex 1 westernmost point is 100 43.1 E, inside the area. VTS-0004 and VRS-0016 match the register.
